name: Christian Democracy
summary: A centrist political tradition rooted in Catholic social teaching and Protestant neo-Calvinism that places the dignity of the human person at the centre of politics. It favours a social market economy with a strong welfare state, class cooperation instead of class conflict, subsidiarity, European integration, and a socially conservative stance on family and life issues, while upholding democracy and religious freedom.
scope: Mainstream post-war European Christian democracy as embodied in the EPP and parties such as the CDU/CSU, drawing on Rerum novarum, Quadragesimo anno, Maritain, Sturzo and Kuyper, with the EPP's 'A Union of Values' as programme. Excludes confessional integralism and the American Solidarity Party's distributism. Many member parties have moved toward market liberalism and, on social issues, are divided.

keyFigures.name: Luigi Sturzo
keyFigures.role: Italian priest who founded the Italian People's Party and developed popularism.

keyFigures.name: Jacques Maritain
keyFigures.role: Philosopher of integral humanism and personalism whose ideas shaped post-war Christian democracy.

keyFigures.name: Konrad Adenauer
keyFigures.role: First West German chancellor and CDU founder, named among the founders of the EPP.

sources.title: Christian democracy
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of positions on economy, family, moral issues, subsidiarity, Europe and thinkers.

sources.title: Rerum novarum (Encyclical of Pope Leo XIII on Capital and Labor, 1891)
sources.author: Pope Leo XIII
sources.usedFor: Founding social encyclical: property, rejection of socialism, class cooperation, unions, just wage, family.

sources.title: Quadragesimo anno (Encyclical of Pope Pius XI on Reconstruction of the Social Order, 1931)
sources.author: Pope Pius XI
sources.usedFor: Subsidiarity, social duty of property, vocational bodies, class conflict, limits of free competition.

sources.title: A Union of Values
sources.author: European People's Party (XIV Congress)
sources.usedFor: Party programme: social market economy, welfare, family, life issues, immigration, EU, education, foreign policy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The EPP programme says all citizens must have access to basic services including healthcare, and the state must meet basic needs where individuals cannot.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Rerum novarum demands a wage that supports a worker and family, but the EPP insists policy must not interfere in wage negotiations between social partners.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Christian democrats back a social market economy with liberalisation and competition, while Quadragesimo anno says free competition cannot by itself direct economic life.

public-ownership.rationale: The EPP urges liberalising or privatising rail, postal, energy and similar sectors, and Rerum novarum rejects state ownership of property in general.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The EPP says European taxation is too high and it intends to reduce it, with no call for soaking the rich.

unions-good.rationale: Rerum novarum praises workers' associations and the EPP calls the social partnership of unions and employers legitimate and useful.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rerum novarum calls private property a natural right, but Quadragesimo anno stresses its social duty and the common good, so it is not absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Adherents want a framework of rules for the market, yet the EPP also pushes to cut regulation for enterprise and SMEs.

cut-welfare.rationale: Christian democrats defend a welfare state and the duty to help the helpless, while favouring reform to curb entitlement mentality.

worker-ownership.rationale: Christian democracy prefers co-determination and class cooperation to collective ownership by workers, and Rerum novarum rejects community of goods.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The EPP calls for stronger police cooperation and efficient joint fighting of terrorism while respecting privacy, from which acceptance of security measures is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Christian democracy is documented as supporting drug prohibition and as treating freedom as bound to responsibility.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The EPP rejects racism and xenophobia and the party backs legal protection of dignity, though no text addresses speech law directly.

strong-leader.rationale: The EPP stresses dialogue, consensus, the rule of law and constitutional checks over personalised leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: Quadragesimo anno rejects the view that the state is a mere guardian of order, and the EPP assigns the state real duties to meet needs.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; mainstream European Christian democracy accepts strict gun controls, inferred from its emphasis on security and rule of law.

empower-police-military.rationale: The EPP demands reinforced police and judicial cooperation and says EU foreign policy must be backed by military resources.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The EPP calls for more rigour against exploitation of prostitution; legalisation is inferred to be disfavoured.

decide-locally.rationale: Subsidiarity, a core principle, puts decisions at the lowest effective level, and the EPP wants a lean Europe resting on local and regional self-governance, though higher bodies act when needed.

rehabilitation.rationale: Christian traditions favour rehabilitation and oppose capital punishment, but the EPP also asks for more rigour against the most dangerous crimes.

traditional-family.rationale: The EPP calls families of fathers and mothers responsible for children the foundation of society, and Rerum novarum defends the family against state absorption.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Christian democracy is documented as socially conservative and sceptical of same-sex marriage, though some parties accept limited legalisation.

abortion-legal.rationale: The EPP protects life from conception to death and refuses to treat abortion as a solution to unwanted pregnancy.

more-religion-public.rationale: Christian democrats defend Christian heritage and ethics in public life and oppose secularisation, while protecting confessional liberty.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Christian democracy rejects racism and exclusion but has no documented programme on correcting historical racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from Catholic social thought and the EPP view of equal but family-centred roles; no direct statement.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The EPP says Europe must safeguard the nation as a way of life and protect national and regional traditions and shared Judeo-Christian heritage.

gradual-change.rationale: Christian democracy rests on dialogue, consensus and reaffirming traditional values, favouring organic rather than radical change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The EPP backs planned, controlled immigration and border surveillance but also open asylum and legal integration, so adherents are split on levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The EPP wants fundamental UN reform, globally binding rules and the EU as a union of nations.

free-trade.rationale: The EPP supports open markets, a single market and opening trade to developing countries, with social and ecological standards in WTO rules.

nation-first.rationale: The EPP says the European project exists to avoid nationalism and that nation states alone cannot safeguard welfare and peace.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The EPP allows military action under UN Charter principles after careful scrutiny and puts human rights in foreign policy; reading is inferred.

open-borders.rationale: The EPP calls for controlled immigration with effective surveillance of external borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The EPP seeks harmony between growth, social development and environment rather than limits on growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Christian democrats emphasise stewardship, and the EPP says the EU must lead the fight against climate change.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Personalism holds science subservient to the human person and the EPP warns against uncritical support for technological development.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and Christian democratic parties differ on nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Christian democracy rejects class struggle and builds on the rule of law, dialogue and consensus.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from the stress on popular participation, democracy and the human person at the centre.

central-planning.rationale: Rerum novarum rejects state-run common ownership and the EPP favours the market economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Christian democracy favours private enterprise and widely held private property over public or worker ownership of firms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the commitment to private property and lower taxes.

basic-income.rationale: The EPP says individuals have a duty to earn a living if they can and links benefits to effort, so unconditional income is inferred to be disfavoured.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from defence of property, family and the aim of reducing taxation.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The EPP opposes subsidies to preserve old jobs and favours opening markets.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The EPP says subsidies are not the way to create jobs and rejects propping up loss-making sectors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Christian democracy defends private property and supports small and natural units of civil society; the American Solidarity Party adopted distributism.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rerum novarum upholds property and a just wage within the existing order and rejects community of goods.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The EPP calls the ECB's independence and price stability vital to the euro.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Quadragesimo anno proposes vocational bodies as organs of the state, but today's parties favour social partnership independent of the state.

one-party-rule.rationale: Democracy, the rule of law and pluralism are core EPP values.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not a Christian democratic issue; parties operate within monarchies and republics alike, so acceptance is inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy and the rule of law are named core values of the EPP and popular participation is central.

direct-votes.rationale: Christian democratic parties work through representative institutions, though the EPP backs e-voting as an option.

workers-councils.rationale: Christian democracy rejects class-based rule and works through parliamentary democracy.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on nation states and union; no direct statement.

natural-rulers.rationale: Human dignity and equality before the law are central, which is inconsistent with a natural right to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Christian democracy draws on pacifist and just-war traditions and builds on consensus, though just-war thinking allows some force.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Quadragesimo anno gives the state the role of protecting the economic and legal order, and the EPP stresses rule of law and common security.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rerum novarum and Quadragesimo anno reject socialism and class conflict, and the EPP is democratic.

conscription.rationale: Christian democratic parties have been divided on conscription, and the sources take no position.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democracy and participation are core values, so the right to vote is not subordinated to exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The EPP says to combat materialistic thinking that reduces the human person to a consumer or client.

organic-representation.rationale: Quadragesimo anno favours vocational bodies, but Christian democracy works through political parties itself.

total-state.rationale: Rerum novarum, subsidiarity and sphere sovereignty all limit the state against family and civil society.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The EPP stands on the rule of law and constitutional democracy.

single-common-good.rationale: The common good is central, and popularism stresses participation of the whole people in it, though pursued through dialogue and consensus.

separated-powers.rationale: The EPP wants constitutional government compatible with the rule of law, subsidiarity and accountability.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The EPP holds that institutions must reflect the will of citizens, directly or indirectly.

vanguard-party.rationale: Christian democracy rejects Marxist class politics and is democratic.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rerum novarum denies class antagonism and Quadragesimo anno gives the state duties toward the common good.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The EPP insists on fundamental rights and the rule of law, though security measures are accepted.

party-controls-media.rationale: Freedom, democracy and the rule of law are core values.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from the rule of law and constitutional democracy, which keep armed forces under the state.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a conventional view of representative office.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the emphasis on the person and on dialogue.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The EPP favours election and representative democracy.

proportional-representation.rationale: Christian democratic parties are documented as linked to proportional representation and consociational democracy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Christian democratic parties are established governing parties and do not hold this populist view.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred from the rule-of-law, rights-based approach of Christian democratic parties, with no direct statement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the stress on the rule of law and human dignity.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Quadragesimo anno rejects the state as a mere guardian of order and the EPP wants the state to meet basic needs.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The dignity of the human person is the central value, with no discrimination accepted.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Just-war thought and state coercion are accepted, so absolute non-aggression is not shared.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not discussed in these terms; Christian democracy ties freedom to responsibility and human dignity.

harm-principle.rationale: Freedom is seen as tied to responsibility and not a license for permissiveness, so the state may restrict beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Personalism and sphere sovereignty recognise the rights of families, churches and associations as well as persons.

positive-liberty.rationale: The EPP says equal opportunity requires access to basic services and the state must meet needs the individual cannot.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: European Christian democracy assumes common civil law, though the EPP lets religious minorities organise on their own background.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The EPP and Christian democracy protect freedom of religion and conscience.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not an issue for the ideology; inferred from freedom of the market and no religious basis for the ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Christian democracy defends parental authority over education and Christian heritage in public life.

separate-church-state.rationale: Christian democrats oppose secularisation and favour cooperation with churches while protecting confessional liberty.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The movement is democratic and pluralist and grounds law in human dignity and natural law, not scripture directly.

war-builds-character.rationale: The EU project is described as a policy of peace to consolidate peace across Europe.

military-superiority.rationale: The EPP wants credible EU and NATO defence capacity but not superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The EPP rejects racism and xenophobia and describes a pluralist European culture.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rerum novarum says capital and labour need each other and class conflict is not natural.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The EPP calls equal opportunity fundamental but stresses personal responsibility and performance.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the preference for development cooperation and trade over reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: The EPP grounds European union in a common cultural and spiritual heritage, though it welcomes enlargement on shared values.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The EPP stresses solidarity and combats materialistic thinking, alongside personal responsibility.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The EPP pairs rights with responsibilities and stresses duty to earn a living and solidarity.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Christian democracy stresses stewardship of creation, with Laudato Si' cited as a major statement.

limit-population.rationale: The EPP wants to reverse falling birth rates through family support, and the Church opposes population control.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The EPP says the 'society of knowledge' and industrial expansion bring gains, with environmental costs to manage.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Science is held subservient to the human person, and the EPP seeks to safeguard what is valuable in civilisation.

human-enhancement.rationale: The EPP rejects politics of unlimited individual self-realisation in bioethics and bans eugenics.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The EPP stresses privacy but also joint action against crime and terrorism; no direct statement.

restore-past-order.rationale: The EPP wants traditional values reaffirmed and modernised and not simply restored.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The EPP says pragmatism and efficiency do not address real concerns and answers must come from values.

direct-action.rationale: Christian democracy works through parties, elections and social partnership.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred from the personalist stress on dignity and dialogue in politics.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contradicts the stress on knowledge, enterprise and heritage of civilisation.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inconsistent with an economy of enterprise and vocational groups.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Quadragesimo anno and the EPP tie reward to work and performance while supporting aid to those in need.

production-for-use.rationale: The EPP endorses enterprise and competition within a social market economy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rerum novarum rejects the claim of class antagonism and stresses cooperation of capital and labour.

collective-farming.rationale: Rerum novarum rejects community of goods and the EPP defends small farms and traditional agriculture.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Christian democracy rejects Marxist theory and the EU is seen as a project of peace through economic integration.

taxation-theft.rationale: The EPP says the state must meet basic needs and has duties under social justice.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The EPP rejects racism and affirms the equal dignity of all.

national-rebirth.rationale: Moderate, centrist tradition with no radical rebirth narrative.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The EPP says the EU exists to avoid nationalism and secure peace.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred from the neo-Thomist and natural-law tradition of truth knowable by reason.

universal-morality.rationale: Christian democracy draws on natural-law thought, Maritain and universal human dignity and rights.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Christian democratic parties are generally supportive of Israel, but this is not covered in these sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; the EPP supports cultural and linguistic diversity.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Christian democracy prefers co-determination, though a public vote on firm governance goes beyond that.

school-vouchers.rationale: The EPP says students must have the right to choose their school and encourages school choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The EPP calls for balanced budgets achieved by lowering expenditure and using surpluses to reduce debt.

economic-freedom.rationale: The EPP couples freedom with freedom of enterprise, though the claim is not stated this strongly.

rule-by-example.rationale: The EPP rests on rule of law and constitutional institutions over ruler example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The EPP honours the nation state as a political form while pooling sovereignty.

force-without-un.rationale: The EPP says action must be taken in accordance with principles of the UN Charter.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Christian democracy rests on Christian roots and values and reconciles faith and reason rather than treating reason alone as the guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The EPP rejects xenophobia and social exclusion and wants legal immigrants integrated, though this is not addressed directly.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The EPP links unemployment benefits to individual effort and says individuals must earn a living if they can.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rerum novarum says capital and labour need each other and Quadragesimo anno calls for ending conflict between classes.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The EPP makes transmitting Europe's humanistic heritage an essential task of education.

dominated-front.rationale: Christian democrats back the Western and transatlantic alliance and cooperation with developing countries.

workers-nation.rationale: Christian democracy rejects class organisation and also seeks European union.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The EPP stresses equality of men and women and the potential of women, despite family-centred views.

ban-interest.rationale: The EPP seeks lower interest rates and better capital markets and accepts modern finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The EPP rejects all forms of racism and discrimination.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from the EPP commitment to the fight against climate change.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The EPP asks immigrants to accept core European values but lets other religious backgrounds organise themselves.

elite-replacement.rationale: The EPP rejects xenophobia and supports planned immigration policy.

national-mission.rationale: Not a Christian democratic theme; the EPP sees Europe as contributing to a better world through union and peace.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The EPP affirms equality of men and women but does not describe society as structured to advantage men.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The EPP says deliberate forms of eugenics must be banned.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The EPP rejects racism and affirms the equal dignity of all persons.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The question presupposes Marxist premises that Christian democracy rejects.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Christian democracy rejects socialist statism and is democratic.

trade-surplus.rationale: The EPP wants strong exports through competitiveness but does not endorse mercantilist surplus targets.

population-transfer.rationale: Contradicts human dignity and the EPP's rejection of exclusion.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The EPP pairs competition with solidarity and rejects struggle as the engine of progress.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Rerum novarum says the poor have a claim to especial consideration and the EPP names the poor and marginalised as a special concern.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred from support for wide property ownership; not addressed directly.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Quadragesimo anno wants strikes forbidden under corporatist bodies, but modern parties stress independence of the social partners.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Christian social teaching blames unjust institutions and wages, and the EPP favours pro-family demographic policy.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The EPP calls Europe a pluralist culture unified by shared values and rejects xenophobia.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from market-economy commitments; the just-price tradition is not invoked by the parties.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The EPP wants planned integration of legal immigrants but names no waiting period.

bound-labor.rationale: Christian democracy upholds free labour, a just wage and human dignity, and rejects bondage of workers.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Christian democrats were founders and chief supporters of European integration, and the EPP programme backs a federal European Union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from the parliamentary systems where Christian democrats mainly govern, with ministers and armed forces answerable to the legislature, and from their commitment to checks and balances.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Christian democratic parties are interconfessional and take no position on how churches are governed, which is left to the churches.

clerical-rule.rationale: The tradition upholds democracy and religious freedom, and its parties are lay political parties, not rule by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: It stands for class cooperation and national and European defense, and rejects class-struggle revolutionary politics.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Socially conservative on family and life, but it upholds freedom and the person's dignity, so general moral censorship of art is inferred as disfavored.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Mostly in parliamentary systems where leaders have no term limits, so presidential limits are not an issue the tradition addressed.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to representative parliamentary democracy; recall is not a feature of Christian democratic programmes.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred: Christian democrats built the EU and the postwar Western alliance and support NATO and security cooperation.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred: the tradition defends private property under social duties and a social market economy, and does not propose banning rentals.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred: mainstream Christian democratic parties back professional armed forces within NATO, not an armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: agrarian and farm-family strands exist in the tradition, but the mainstream does not hold rural life morally superior.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred: Christian democrats such as Kohl led German reunification, though the tradition has no general doctrine on divided nations.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: Christian democracy is a broad centrist tradition with strong university-educated leadership and no anti-intellectual strand.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred: the tradition rests on universal human dignity under natural law, and many member parties stress a Christian-rooted common culture over cultural equivalence.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred: the Church and European Christian democratic parties generally oppose capital punishment, but it is not a defining tenet.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: parties support schooling and gender equality but stress parental rights and family values, so adherents split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: Christian democrats uphold religion in public life but mainstream parties accept evolution in school science.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred: social conservatism on family and morals typical of the tradition favors some legal limits on pornography.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred: German and other member parties have moved between descent-based and territorial rules and are divided.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred: subsidiarity and respect for communities favor protecting minority languages, as CDU/CSU and other parties do for Sorbs or South Tyrol.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred: the EPP programme and Christian democracy uphold religious freedom as a core value, which favors accommodating minority religions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred: the tradition emphasizes social bonds, family and moral order over celebrating nonconformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Catholic teaching has backed debt relief for the poorest, but the EPP stresses fiscal responsibility, so adherents split; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Christian democracy seeks class cooperation and reform within a social market economy, not transformation of the property system; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Post-war parties built on constitutional continuity and amendment by existing procedures; inferred from that practice.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The EPP programme grounds politics in human dignity, democracy and fundamental freedoms, which are not traded for growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Catholic social teaching holds that goods are meant for all, and the EPP programme supports development cooperation with poor countries.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Mainstream parties rely on NATO and European integration for defence rather than national deterrents; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Parties split: Germany and Italy use indirect election while Austria and France elect presidents directly; the tradition has no doctrine.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The EPP programme supports a stable euro and sound public finances, which is consistent with price-stability-focused central banks; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Christian democracy favours negotiated settlements and peace over territorial maximalism; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Quadragesimo anno holds that property has a social as well as an individual character and that its use must serve the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Christian democracy saw the USSR as a totalitarian communist state and rejected socialism, so it would not endorse the state-capitalist label; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from stewardship of creation and the EPP commitment to sustainability; precaution itself is not stated.

collective-defense.rationale: EPP parties back NATO and mutual defense as a core of European security policy.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: the EPP stresses international law and territorial integrity, so annexation without consent is not accepted.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Rerum novarum defends the Church's own rights and property, and the programme upholds religious freedom, so state control of the clergy is rejected.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: Christian democracy works within parliamentary democracies where the head of state is usually a unifying figure above parties.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred: the tradition prefers legal and peaceful settlement and democratic consent, though it also stresses territorial integrity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Subsidiarity places decisions at the lowest competent level, which favors regional autonomy within a state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The tradition upholds democracy and the dignity of the person; a sacred ruler of divine descent has no place in it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the social market economy and welfare state favor progressive taxation, though some member parties support flatter taxes.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; Christian thought stresses both formation by family and education and a given human nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Christian democracy is a democratic and rule-of-law tradition, so rulers are bound by law.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed; the parties work within constitutional democracies and subsidiarity but do not advocate a mixed constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader worship conflicts with the democratic and personalist commitments of the tradition.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred: parties are divided between family-protective and equality-of-parents positions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Christian democracy favours class cooperation over class conflict, as the overview documents; the socialism question is inferred from that.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rerum novarum defends private property as a natural right and rejects redistribution schemes, though wide ownership is favoured.

refugee-return.rationale: Return of refugees is not a defining question and parties differ; neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Christian democracy is committed to European integration and peace between nations; inferred opposition to border claims by nationality.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Christian democracy upholds democracy and religious freedom, which excludes penalties for leaving a religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Christian democracy upholds dignity of the person and religious freedom, which excludes legal compulsion to cover.

common-currency.rationale: Christian democratic parties built and defend European integration; the EPP programme supports closer union, including the euro.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Christian democracy emphasises integration of nations in a federal Europe rather than ethnic unions; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Subsidiarity, from Quadragesimo anno, supports self-governing intermediate bodies; inferred support for minority autonomy within states.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Christian democracy stresses person dignity and equal rights in democratic states; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Christian democracy rejects Marxist materialism and puts the human person and moral values at the centre.

ban-cartels.rationale: The social market economy tradition relies on competition policy to keep markets open.

no-bailouts.rationale: Parties have both rescued banks and defended market discipline, but social-market rules favour limits; inferred weakly.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Christian democracy upholds liberal democracy with rule of law and rights; inferred opposition to unbounded majority rule.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Parties are divided on quotas, with some adopting them and others opposed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Christian democracy favours European integration and a social market economy open to trade, not autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: A social market economy with solidarity suggests support for social standards in trade; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: The programme accepts market incentives within a social market economy; inferred, though solidarity is stressed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Christian democracy is a democratic, anti-revolutionary tradition that works through elections.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Parties operate in both monarchies and republics and the question is not central; neutral.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Not a defining issue; Christian democrats emphasise European and Christian heritage but are divided on national-centred curricula.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to human dignity and equality of peoples in the EPP programme; colonial paternalism is not endorsed.

patriotic-education.rationale: Adherents are divided between national-conservative parties that favour it and more European-minded ones.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Parties are divided; the tradition stresses human dignity and non-discrimination but also social-market merit-based policy.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from the social market economy's acceptance of independent banking and private markets; not addressed directly.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The social market economy and Catholic social teaching aim to reform capitalism by social cooperation rather than expect its collapse.

delink-world-market.rationale: The EPP programme favours integration and open markets, so breaking economic ties is rejected.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Christian democracy rejects Marxist class analysis in favour of class cooperation; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the centrality of human dignity and non-discrimination and from religious freedom; not stated for private association specifically.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's defence of human dignity, rule of law and fundamental rights; the question of entrenchment is not stated.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Christian democrats have no common position on past colonial borders; inferred as split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Christian democrats uphold democracy and several parties sit in constitutional monarchies, so they are split on the hereditary throne.

minority-veto.rationale: Christian democracy supports majority rule in democracy with protections for minorities and subsidiarity, not a veto for every dissenter; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Catholic tradition accepts resistance to a ruler who breaks law and justice, and the EPP stands for the rule of law; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Christian democratic parties govern in parliamentary democracies and uphold them in 'A Union of Values'; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Christian democrats stress human dignity and stewardship of creation, so animal suffering counts morally; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The tradition allows human use of animals under stewardship and without cruelty; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Rerum novarum teaches that the wealthy owe charity from their surplus and fair dealing to workers, which Christian democracy inherits.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Christian democracy sees political participation as part of the common good; inferred rejection of withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The sources stress human dignity and a free civil society and do not endorse a pacification theory; inferred rejection.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Christian democracy accepts that culture and institutions shape consent, but it does not use the class-hegemony framing; no clear answer.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Christian democracy backs international solidarity and development cooperation within a social market economy rather than a surplus-extraction thesis; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Christian democracy upholds equal dignity and European integration; reserving offices for natives is inferred to be rejected.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist parties are outside Christian democracy's concerns; no stance can be drawn.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Christian democracy stresses solidarity and European integration and supports aid and cooperation; inferred rejection of self-reliance only.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Christian democracy founded European integration on postwar reconciliation; inferred rejection of demands for lost territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Christian democracy upholds equal citizenship and the dignity of every person; inferred rejection of rule by descent.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Postwar Christian democracy was built against Nazi and fascist rule, so inferred support, though not stated as a founding principle.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The EPP and postwar Christian democrats opposed both Nazi and communist dictatorship; inferred support for joint condemnation.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The American Civil War is outside the sources; inferred from respect for human dignity that slavery was central.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Christian democrats are split between respect for tradition and condemnation of the figures; no common position.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Christian democracy holds family and gender roles in tension and is divided on this question.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The doctrine of human dignity implies protection for any victim of domestic violence; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: A Union of Values presents democracy, human rights and the rule of law as universal; inferred rejection.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Christian democratic parties uphold civilian democratic control of the armed forces; inferred strong rejection of a political guardian role.

paid-care-work.rationale: Christian democracy backs family policy and recognition of caring work, though payment as labour is not a stated position; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: The family is the core social unit in Rerum novarum and the EPP programme, and Catholic teaching treats care for parents as a family duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: Christian democrats accept a professional civil service but also value elected office; the tradition has no settled view on exams versus election, inferred from its democratic principles.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The EPP backs an open single market but member parties differ on screening strategic investments; inferred from its social market stance.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The EPP programme is socially conservative on marriage and family, so most adherents prefer divorce to require grounds or a process, though many parties accepted divorce reform; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The EPP upholds representative parliamentary democracy with free mandates, so binding and instantly recallable delegates is inferred to be rejected.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Christian democracy stresses solidarity and a state-backed welfare system, and postwar parties built pay-as-you-go pensions; fully private accounts are inferred to be rejected.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Rerum novarum defends private property as a natural right and rejects collective ownership of land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Christian democracy is committed to parliamentary democracy and the rule of law, so parliamentary control of spending is inferred as accepted.

single-official-language.rationale: The EPP supports cultural and linguistic diversity and subsidiarity, so a restrictive sole-language policy is inferred to be disfavoured.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The EPP favours the single market and free movement of capital, so a blanket ban on foreign land ownership is inferred to be disfavoured.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Christian democracy stresses equal dignity of persons and individual responsibility, not outcome-based tests of discrimination; inferred from its principles.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Catholic social teaching in Quadragesimo anno criticises unbridled acquisitiveness, so adherents are inferred to see consumerism as harmful.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The EPP programme stresses international law and democratic values, so covertly arming insurgents is inferred to be disfavoured.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The EPP stresses democracy, sovereignty and self-determination of states, so forcible intervention to stop an ally leaving is inferred to be rejected.

corporate-influence.rationale: Christian democrats favour a social market economy with active business as well as labour; the programme sets no stance on lobbying, so adherents are split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: mainstream Christian democracy upholds open civil society, though some member parties have pushed such limits.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the family-centred, socially conservative stance and support for family policy; the sources do not rank it against immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: free movement of capital and property within the European single market that Christian democrats back makes residence-only purchases unlikely to be supported.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: the social market economy relies on private employment with social insurance rather than a state employer of last resort.

democratic-peace.rationale: The EPP programme presents promoting democracy and human rights abroad as the basis of a peaceful European and global order.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: Christian democracy upholds the rule of law and respect for legitimate authority, while allowing conscientious resistance to unjust laws.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: the EPP supports international action to protect human rights and stop atrocities, which rules out an absolute ban on intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Catholic social teaching backs workers associations and unions without prescribing industrial over craft form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Human dignity and equality before the law are central to Christian democracy, and the EPP programme opposes antisemitism and discrimination.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage as a legal institution is part of the socially conservative family stance of Christian democracy.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the EPP commitment to open, accountable government and the rule of law; the sources do not state a right of access.

local-production.rationale: Subsidiarity favours local decisions, but the EPP backs the single market, so local production is not a stated aim.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: Christian democratic politics works through parties, unions and church bodies, with subsidiarity favouring many associations, not only informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The EPP supports European integration and pooled sovereignty, accepting EU law and courts above national law.

religious-nation.rationale: Mainstream Christian democracy upholds religious freedom and democracy, and the scope excludes confessional integralism.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Christian democracy stresses the equal dignity of persons and peoples and a rules-based order, so ritual submission to a leading power is inferred as contrary.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The tradition's principle of solidarity favours sharing between regions, and EPP parties generally support fiscal equalisation and EU cohesion funds, though some regional parties dissent.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Rerum novarum defends private property as a natural right and rejects socialist common ownership of the means of production, so the statement's second half is opposed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Rerum novarum rejects socialism and post-war Christian democrats were committed anti-communists and Cold War Atlanticists, though most accept coexistence and diplomacy.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The social market model and subsidiarity favour private, church-run and voluntary providers delivering welfare services within publicly funded systems, as in German welfare associations.

religion-illusion.rationale: Christian democracy is rooted in the Christian faith and treats religion as answering lasting human needs, so the illusion thesis is firmly rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The tradition accepts market capitalism within a social market economy but criticises its excesses, and does not teach a view on capitalism's historical role, so adherents are split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Christian democrats generally hold that equality for women can be reached by law, education and family policy within a social market economy, and reject the Marxist view of economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Subsidiarity and the emphasis on the family as the basic unit mean care is best done in families with support, not as replacement public services, though childcare provision is accepted.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The mainstream tradition does not call for linguistic purism, and pro-European Christian democrats favour open cultural exchange; this is inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Christian democracy's respect for law and agreements makes binding treaties likely, though the tradition has no explicit position on treaties with internal nations; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Christian democracy supports private property, the nation-state and the EU, and not communal property; the Catholic tradition rejects common ownership as a model for society.

majority-settlement.rationale: Christian democracy upholds minority rights and subsidiarity, and the EPP programme supports protecting national minorities, so state-steered majority settlement is rejected.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rerum novarum and Quadragesimo anno reject both unrestrained liberal capitalism and socialism, and Christian democracy is defined as a middle course such as the social market economy.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the movement's postwar commitment to European integration and borders by consent, not historical claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Postwar Christian democracy was founded on rejecting Nazism and totalitarianism and on human dignity.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Mainstream parties are socially conservative on family but uphold democracy and personal rights; the sources do not call for criminalisation; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Christian democracy upholds democracy, pluralism and independent civic organisations.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The EPP programme upholds religious freedom, and Christian democrats do not call for punishing blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on human dignity and European values in the programme; colonial rule is not defended.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Christian democracy upholds democracy and religious freedom and does not allow force against secular rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Subsidiarity favours decisions at the lowest level, but through representative institutions; split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Christian democracy stresses class cooperation and the person, not an overlapping-oppressions theory; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Socially conservative on family; member parties are divided, with the majority cautious; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: The programme defends the protection of human life at all stages.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Christian democracy places itself in the centre, combining ideas, but does not call the division obsolete; split.

alienated-labor.rationale: Christian democracy criticises unrestrained capitalism but not with the Marxist alienation concept; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Member parties are divided between identity concerns and Christian-heritage openness; the programme addresses immigration only generally.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Christian democracy rests on Catholic natural-law teaching and Christian values, while accepting democracy; inferred as a majority view.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious freedom and Christian heritage lead mainstream parties to oppose bans on religious dress; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Christian democracy explicitly stands for a social market economy with welfare state and competition rules.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The programme supports NATO and EU defence cooperation, not abolition of armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Christian democracy stresses solidarity and the social duty of property, so not letting some grow rich first; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The EPP programme is Atlanticist and committed to NATO alliance and the EU.

missingStatements.text: Public decisions should be taken at the lowest level that can handle them, with higher bodies stepping in only when lower ones cannot.
missingStatements.rationale: Subsidiarity is stated in Quadragesimo anno and listed as a core EPP value.

missingStatements.text: Nations should pool part of their sovereignty in a supranational union such as the European Union.
missingStatements.rationale: The EPP says nation states alone cannot safeguard welfare and peace and calls Europe both a means and an end in itself.

missingStatements.text: The death penalty should be abolished.
missingStatements.rationale: Christian democracy is documented as opposing capital punishment as part of a consistent life ethic.
missingStatements.declined: Documented only as a secondary position and not a defining one; kept out to keep the bank lean.

notes: Parties differ widely: southern and eastern European members are more socially conservative and the American Solidarity Party leans distributist, while many northern parties embraced neoliberal economics from the 1980s and accept limited abortion and civil partnerships. Quadragesimo anno's corporatism is largely historical.
